title: Former Chief Executive Officer and Founder at Arkona Home Robotics Believes Broadly Capable Humanoid Robots Are Still Three to Five Years Away
expert: Former CEO and founder of Arkona Home Robotics, now consultant; hands-on with robotics models on small arms; no NVIDIA purchase data; interview 2026-11-10
verdict: A former home-robotics founder sees NVIDIA's Cosmos 3 as a generic starting model, with broadly capable humanoids still three to five years away; the call gives no near-term NVIDIA revenue signal.

Demand / orders (physical AI): 🟡 **Broadly capable humanoids 3-5 years away** (estimate), gated by tactile sensing and precise actuators; first read on humanoid timing. → Tenet 4 (new TAM vectors) →
🟡 **Biggest Cosmos models need 32 GB RAM or two GPUs; on-site fine-tuning runs on a single GPU** (estimate): modest per-site compute.
Competition & share: 🟢 **NVIDIA is the "primary enabler"** via chips and Cosmos; learning does not transfer across sites, so value sits in local fine-tuning.

characterization_changed: Characterization changed from Positive: the expert quantifies no NVIDIA demand and puts broadly capable humanoids 3-5 years out; NVIDIA is an enabler only.
changes: First read on humanoid-robot timing and Cosmos compute needs; no earlier expert call or stored row.
thesis_impact: Tenet 4 (new TAM vectors): → — physical AI is 3-5 years from broad capability; NVIDIA is the enabler (Cosmos, chips) but no revenue is quantified.
